primarySuggestion.name: Case-hardening steel (drawing calls 20MnCr5 / 1.7147 — closest catalogue match is mat-steel1045; exact grade not in the valid materialId list)
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Drawing MATERIAL field explicitly states 20MnCr5 (1.7147), a European case-hardening steel, with HEAT TREATMENT = CARBURISE + QUENCH, case depth 0.6-0.9mm, 58-62 HRC. None of the valid materialId values is a case-hardening steel grade; mat-steel1045 is the nearest medium-carbon steel proxy commonly substituted for costing case-hardened gear steels. True 20MnCr5 costs somewhat more per kg than 1045 — flag this substitution to the customer.

alternatives.name: Stainless bar stock (not indicated by drawing, listed only as a generic steel alternative)
Austempered ductile iron (not indicated — drawing clearly specifies wrought case-hardening steel)

processRecommendations.reasoning: Drawing calls ISO 1328 class 7 with carburise+quench heat treatment. Class 7 cannot reliably be held through case-hardening distortion without a post-HT finishing grind on the tooth flanks; hobbing alone (uncorrected) typically lands class 8-9 after HT.

processRecommendations.process: Carburise + quench + temper (batch furnace, case depth 0.6-0.9mm)
processRecommendations.reasoning: Placeholder commodityType — this is an outsourced heat-treat furnace operation, not covered by the machineId list; cost/cycle should be handled as a subcontract line rather than a CNC operation.

processRecommendations.process: CMM/gear inspection (lead, profile, pitch) to ISO 1328 class 7
processRecommendations.reasoning: Class 7 quality callout requires sampling inspection on a gear-checking device / CMM, adding non-cutting time per batch.

manufacturabilityRisks.feature: Tooth flank quality vs heat-treat distortion
manufacturabilityRisks.description: Case-hardening (carburise+quench) at 58-62 HRC surface will distort the tooth form; holding ISO 1328 class 7 as-drawn typically requires post-HT gear grinding, not just hobbing/shaving.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Confirm with customer whether class 7 is measured before or after heat treatment; budget a generation-grinding op if post-HT.

manufacturabilityRisks.feature: Bore Ø40 H7 after heat treat
manufacturabilityRisks.description: H7 bore tolerance is tight relative to carburise/quench distortion; bore may need to be finish-bored or ground after heat treatment to hold H7.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Sequence: rough bore before HT, finish bore/ream after HT, or induction-mask the bore to avoid case hardening it.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: B-rep threading detection flags a threaded feature that does not appear on the supplied drawing sheet.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Verify with design office whether an ancillary drawing (e.g. hub/shaft interface) defines this thread; do not silently ignore or silently cost it in.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Case depth is specified as a 0.6-0.9mm range rather than a single value; carburising furnace time scales with ECD², so quoting at the low end (0.6) vs high end (0.9) changes furnace time by ~2.25x.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Use mid-band 0.75mm for costing but confirm target with metallurgy before final quote.

dfmIssues.description: Carburise + quench to 58-62 HRC will distort tooth form; ISO 1328 class 7 tolerance is tight relative to typical as-carburised distortion.
dfmIssues.impact: May require an added gear-grinding operation post-HT, adding ~10-15 min/part and grinder tooling cost.
dfmIssues.fix: Clarify whether class 7 applies pre- or post-heat-treatment; if post-HT, add generation grinding to the process plan and quote accordingly.

dfmIssues.description: Tight H7 bore tolerance combined with carburise/quench thermal distortion risks out-of-tolerance bore after heat treat.
dfmIssues.impact: Scrap/rework risk if bore is carburised and distorts; extra finishing operation needed.
dfmIssues.fix: Copper-plate or ream/finish-bore the bore after heat treatment; consider bore masking to prevent case hardening in the bore if not required functionally.

dfmIssues.description: Geometry kernel detects a threaded feature not documented on the attached drawing sheet.
dfmIssues.impact: Undocumented feature could be mis-costed or omitted from the manufacturing plan.
dfmIssues.fix: Confirm with design office whether a companion drawing defines this thread (e.g., shaft/hub retention); do not assume it away.

dfmIssues.description: Case depth given as a range rather than single value; carburising time scales as ECD², so cost is sensitive to which end of the band is targeted.
dfmIssues.impact: Furnace time (and cost) could vary up to ~2x between 0.6mm and 0.9mm target.
dfmIssues.fix: Confirm target case depth with metallurgy/design before final quote; mid-band 0.75mm used for this estimate.

dfmIssues.description: At 200,000 units/year (16,670/month batches), dedicated gear-hobbing and grinding tooling with automated load/unload would materially reduce per-part cycle time versus the generic VMC-based CNC estimate used here.
dfmIssues.impact: Generic CNC-derived cycle time (0.817hr) is conservative for a dedicated high-volume gear cell; true unit cost at this volume is likely lower.
dfmIssues.fix: Recommend a dedicated hobbing + shaving/grinding cell with automated fixturing for this annual volume rather than general-purpose VMC machining.

analysis.aiExplanation: The attached drawing (GT-38-M3 Rev B) fully corroborates the measured B-rep geometry: 38 teeth, 3mm normal module, 30mm face width. The drawing specifies material 20MnCr5 (1.7147) with carburise+quench heat treatment to 58-62 HRC surface hardness and 0.6-0.9mm effective case depth, plus ISO 1328 quality class 7. Since no exact case-hardening steel grade exists in the valid materialId catalogue, mat-steel1045 has been substituted as the closest match and flagged for customer review. The process plan reflects hob-then-post-HT-grind sequencing to reliably hold class 7 through heat-treat distortion, plus a post-HT bore finish to protect the Ø40 H7 tolerance. A threaded feature detected in the B-rep but absent from the drawing has been flagged as a discrepancy for design-office confirmation rather than silently included or excluded from costing.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for gear from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • gear.teeth = 38 — counted 38 tip-circle patch(es) at r≈60.0 mm clustered to 38 angular positions [geometry, gear-teeth]
  • gear.helixAngleDeg = 0 — spur — 0° helix (assumed — confirm before quoting) [engineer, gear-helix]
  • gear.normalModuleMm = 3 — mn = tip Ø 120.0 / (z 38 + 2) = 3.00 mm — standard addendum; recon 120.0 mm vs measured OD 120.0 mm (assumed — confirm before quoting) [geometry, gear-module]
  • gear.faceWidthMm = 30 — axial span of the tip-land patches = 30.0 mm [geometry, gear-face]
  • gear.internal = false — tip patches face outward — external gear [geometry, gear-internal]
  • gear.qualityClass = 7 — ISO 1328 class 7 (assumed — confirm before quoting) [engineer, gear-quality]
  • gear.effectiveCaseDepthMm = 0.7 — no case depth stated — using the 0.70 mm reference the cycle times are built around. Carburising time scales as ECD², so a drawing calling 1.2 mm costs roughly 3x the furnace time of one calling 0.7 mm; take it off the drawing before quoting. [library, gear-ecd]
  • gear.batchSize = 16670 — monthly delivery batches: 200,000/yr ÷ 12 [rule, gear-batch]

Still open (1):
  • What is the gear cut from? — The solid weighs the same in 20MnCr5 and 42CrMo4, so the CAD cannot tell a carburised gear from a through-hardened one — and the choice changes the heat-treat route, the finishing route and the feeds the teeth are cut at.
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: What is the gear cut from?
No DFM analyser exists for gear; an empty issue list here means "not checked", not "nothing found".

decisions.question: What is the gear cut from?
decisions.why: The solid weighs the same in 20MnCr5 and 42CrMo4, so the CAD cannot tell a carburised gear from a through-hardened one — and the choice changes the heat-treat route, the finishing route and the feeds the teeth are cut at. The model read "case_hardening_steel" off the drawing/context — confirm or correct it before it reaches the costing.

options.label: Through-hardening steel (42CrMo4 / EN19)
options.consequence: quench + temper; distortion lower than carburising

options.label: Pre-hardened alloy steel (~30 HRC)
options.consequence: no post-cut heat treat; slower cutting feeds

options.consequence: cut soft or moulded; no heat treat
